On 4 August 2015 at 05:58, Andy Martin <and...@zillow.com> wrote:

Hi Dr. Southworth,

 

My colleagues and I here at Zillow have been looking into the monotonic trees feature in your GBM package.  We haven’t been able to find a published algorithm or slide about how you enforce this though I was able to find a code fragment in the C++ code.  Not have written C++ before I wanted to verify that we had identified the algorithm correctly as:

 

IF (split is a continuous variable and monotonic)

THEN take average of left and right child nodes if current split is used

   IF monotonic increasing THEN CHECK left average <= right average

   IF monotonic decreasing THEN CHECK left average >= right average

This seems like the intuitive thing to do and should work for any tree based model but since the code fragment I found is an online version where observations are added and not the main split search (best I could tell) I wanted to verify.

 

Thanks for you time and work to make such a great package!

 

Andrew Martin
Sr. Data Scientist

messages.author: 519907adbbc83e48
messages.subject: Re: Monotonic Trees Algo in GBM
parts:
Basically if the monotone option is set, then it only considers splits for which the predictions in the right and left nodes are consistent with the desired direction of monotonicity. If they're not, the algorithm just doesn't consider it a candidate and moves on.

Note that this just enforces monotonicity locally. It's possible that nodes in other parts of the tree might create a violation of the overall monotonicity.

Greg
